facts.meaning: The replica records the ballot it has promised and uses it to qualify incoming acceptance work.
facts.validity_context: Current replica instance and stored promise; matching promise is necessary but role, phase and sequence may add guards.
facts.durability: Written through Storage; actual durability is backend-dependent.
facts.recovery: Loaded from backend; nonempty promise starts recovery preparation.

facts.meaning: The leader records the latest assigned accepted index for each node in its current LeaderState.
facts.validity_context: Current LeaderState; an index is local accounting, not independently a new decision or proof of current follower reachability.
facts.durability: Volatile; a new LeaderState zeros indexes.
facts.recovery: Rebuilt through local synchronization and incoming Accepted messages.
unknowns: Same-ballot reconnect leaves previous indexes in place; determine why these remain valid under permitted crash and transport histories.

facts.meaning: The local decided index marks the prefix exported as decided, including a decided StopSign when present.

formation.explanation: Caller append buffers or forwards until a leader is in Accept. The leader gathers matching per-node promises to a configured preparation quorum, selects maximum accepted round/length and maximum decided index, installs history, and synchronizes promised followers. Local appends update self support and emit AcceptDecide. Followers with matching promise, phase and sequence persist accepted entries and reply. Leader handle_accepted records sender support; a configured acceptance quorum at a larger index advances its decided prefix and propagates Decide or coalesced metadata. Followers advance decided state with batch handling; reads label entries below that index as Decided.

context.explanation: BLE heartbeat rounds and manual takeover nominate ballots. SequencePaxos acquires local preparation authority only above its prior leader and promise. Prepare flushes pending writes, persists the promise, resets receive sequence and returns accepted history. Matching promises enable transition to Accept. Higher Prepare changes follower authority; old-ballot acceptance is rejected with NotAccepted, unexplained future ballots and sequence gaps request recovery, outdated sequenced messages are ignored. Restart with stored promise enters Recover; reconnect and timer paths repeat preparation. A StopSign accepted as final entry blocks new appends, and its decision allows caller-created next-configuration instances.

connection.explanation: Authority changes constrain which accepted history can become new support: promises report accepted round/length and existing decision index; maximal history is installed before new proposals are accepted. Follower synchronization retains a prefix based on matching accepted rounds or decided history, then starts a new sequence session. A new leader resets volatile support; recovery retains persisted history and cannot simply reuse ordinary acceptance phase. Old-ballot messages are rejected, while same-ballot late promises trigger follower synchronization. Buffered ordinary proposals are appended by a winning leader or forwarded after follower sync unless sealed. Prior StopSign travels with history and blocks further appends. Same-ballot delayed replies, configuration routing and buffered StopSign transfer remain localized unresolved premises.
